title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: grave charge — if our sentence uproots Christianity's foundations it must itself be uprooted; we grant their double-love foundation but deny our sentence fights it
pass_a_gloss: Truly this crime which is objected unto us is grave. For if our sentence uproots the foundations of the Christian religion, it is itself indeed to be torn up from the lowest foundations. Let us therefore weigh how true this accusation is. And first we intend no quarrel with the adversaries concerning that twofold love in which they place the foundation of religion; but we deny that our sentence fights against this love.
pass_b_english: Truly this charge against us is grave. If our view uproots Christianity's foundations, it must itself be torn up from the roots. So let us weigh how true the accusation is. First: we pick no quarrel with the adversaries over that twofold love in which they set religion's foundation — but we deny that our view fights that love.
source_text: Grave profecto hoc crimen est quod nobis objicitur. Nam si sententia nostra convellat religionis Christianae fundamenta, est ipsa quidem ab imis fundamentis revellenda. Expendamus igitur quam vera sit haec criminatio. Atque inprimis non intendimus ullam litem adversariis de duplici illo amore in quo religionis fundamentum collocant; sed negamus sententiam nostram huic amori repugnare.
